answer: Coordination Price Curve. Each new agent identity must acquire a unique coordination token whose price rises along a fixed curve toward a zenith as the active identity count grows; the payment is non-refundable and routed to existing agents. Registering many identities therefore costs a steeply increasing sum. The curve's slope sets the dune line above which an attacker's marginal cost exceeds any gain from one extra vote. Because every token also reserves bandwidth on the shared ocean of message capacity, mass registration degrades the attacker's own throughput,
